question: What is the biggest hurdle nurses face when handling emergency deliveries in rural community clinics?

options.A: An excessive number of available medical doctors on site
options.B: Lack of immediate access to specialized surgical care and blood banks
options.C: Patients refusing to take prescribed oral medications
options.D: Strict hospital policies preventing any intervention

explanation: Rural clinics often lack advanced surgery and blood supplies, making quick stabilization and fast transfer super important to save lives! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h1)

question: Why is spotting delivery complications early at a primary health centre so crucial?

options.A: It ensures the family will pay the delivery fees on time
options.B: It guarantees the baby will be born without any health issues
options.C: It allows the nurse to intervene or arrange transfer before full collapse happens
options.D: It completely stops the normal labor process from continuing

explanation: Catching warning signs early gives you precious time to start emergency steps and move the mother safely before things get out of hand. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h1)

question: Which sign strongly points to severe pre-eclampsia in a pregnant mum?

options.A: Painful urination and cloudy urine output
options.B: Itchy skin on the palms and soles of the feet
options.D: Sudden severe headache and high blood pressure

explanation: High BP combined with a terrible headache or vision changes is a classic red flag for severe pre-eclampsia. Keep your eyes peeled for this! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h2)

question: A mum who delivered an hour ago at a primary clinic has soaked three maternity pads in 30 minutes and feels dizzy. What's going on?
explanation: Soaking pads rapidly plus dizziness means heavy bleeding (PPH). She needs quick intervention right away! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h2)

question: You feel the uterus and it is soft and boggy right after delivery. What is your very first action?

options.A: Apply warm compresses to the lower back
options.C: Transfer the patient to a tertiary hospital immediately

explanation: Massage helps the uterine muscles tighten up and clamp down on bleeding vessels. It's a quick, lifesaving first step! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h3)

question: Why does passing a urinary catheter help when managing postpartum hemorrhage?

options.A: It completely stops the flow of blood from the vagina
options.B: A full bladder stops the uterus from contracting effectively
options.C: It allows the nurse to measure exact urine output
options.D: It prevents the patient from getting a urinary tract infection

explanation: An overfull bladder pushes the uterus out of place so it can't contract properly. Empty it out, and the uterus can firm up! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h3)

question: What is the go-to medication used to stop and prevent seizures in severe pre-eclampsia?
explanation: Magnesium sulfate is our absolute best friend for preventing and stopping eclamptic fits. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h4)

question: What should you do immediately when a pregnant woman starts having an eclamptic seizure?

options.A: Hold her arms and legs tightly straight to stop the shaking
options.B: Force a wooden spatula between her teeth to hold the airway open
options.C: Leave the room quickly to call for an ambulance doctor
options.D: Turn her onto her side and protect her from physical injury

explanation: Placing her in the recovery position keeps her airway clear and safe from choking. Never force anything into her mouth! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h4)

question: What happens during the McRoberts maneuver when dealing with shoulder dystocia?

options.A: The mother's thighs are flexed sharply toward her abdomen
options.B: The mother is turned completely onto her hands and knees
options.C: Firm pressure is applied directly on top of the mother's fundus
options.D: The nurse pulls gently on the baby's head to release the shoulder

explanation: Pulling her knees right up to her chest changes the pelvis angle and helps pop that stuck shoulder free without pulling on the baby. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h5)

question: Why is pushing down on top of the mother's bump (fundal pressure) a big no-no during shoulder dystocia?

options.A: It stops the placenta from delivering after the baby
options.B: It makes the baby turn around into a breech position
options.C: It causes the mother's blood pressure to drop too low
options.D: It can cause the trapped shoulder to wedge tighter and rupture the uterus

explanation: Pushing from above only jams the shoulder harder against the bone. Avoid fundal pressure completely in shoulder dystocia! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h5)

question: What is your immediate priority action if the umbilical cord slips out (prolapses) during labor?

options.A: Manually lift the baby's head off the cord to restore blood flow
options.B: Push the visible cord gently back inside the uterine cavity
options.C: Clamp and cut the umbilical cord immediately on the spot
options.D: Instruct the mother to push as hard as she can with contractions

explanation: Keeping pressure off the cord with your hand keeps oxygen flowing to the baby while you prep for urgent delivery. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h6)

question: Which sign strongly suggests a pregnant woman's uterus has ruptured during a difficult labor?

options.A: A gradual increase in contractions with steady pink show
options.B: Sudden sharp tearing pain and disappearance of contractions
options.C: High fever accompanied by foul-smelling vaginal discharge
options.D: Mild lower backache that improves when walking around

explanation: If contractions suddenly stop after a sharp, tearing pain, think uterine rupture. It's a major emergency! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h6)

question: What is the very first step in newborn resuscitation if a baby doesn't cry or breathe right after birth?

options.A: Dry thoroughly with warm towels and provide stimulation
options.B: Administer emergency intravenous drugs through the umbilical cord
options.C: Submerge the baby briefly in warm water to shock the system
options.D: Give chest compressions at a rate of 120 beats per minute

explanation: Drying and rubbing the baby warms them up and gives just enough stimulation to get them breathing on their own. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h7)

question: How often should you check a mother's vital signs while she is stabilizing after a postpartum hemorrhage?
explanation: Checking every 15 minutes lets you catch early signs of shock or ongoing bleeding before they become life-threatening. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h7)

question: What essential document must go with a patient when transferring her from a clinic to a bigger hospital during an emergency?

options.A: A blank sheet of paper for the hospital doctors to sign
options.B: A clear referral note detailing interventions and vital signs
options.C: A detailed receipt of all community clinic registration fees
options.D: The patient's birth certificate and marriage license

explanation: A solid referral note tells the hospital team what you've done so far and why she's being sent. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h8)

question: Why should a nurse accompany a critically ill maternity patient during transit to a hospital?

options.A: To drive the transport vehicle if the driver gets tired
options.B: To negotiate hospital admission fees with the receiving clerk
options.C: To bring back empty medical equipment to the local clinic
options.D: To monitor ongoing treatment and handle sudden emergencies on the way

explanation: Having a nurse onboard means IV lines, bleeding, and breathing are watched closely every step of the journey. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h8)

question: What should NOT be included in professional clinical notes after an emergency?

options.A: Exact timelines of all emergency interventions performed
options.B: Medication names, exact dosages, and administration times
options.C: The patient's physical response to the medical treatment
options.D: Personal opinions about the patient's family behavior

explanation: Keep notes strictly factual and professional. Leave out personal opinions or judgements about family members. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h9)

question: Why do nursing teams hold a quick debriefing session after handling a stressful emergency?

options.A: To celebrate the end of the working shift with refreshments
options.B: To fill out insurance claim forms for hospital equipment use
options.C: To review performance, share feelings, and identify areas to improve
options.D: To assign blame to the junior nurse who made a mistake

explanation: Debriefing is a safe space to decompress, process emotions, and learn how the team can work even better next time. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h9)
